one_line: A Lovevery tummy-time tip filmed on a play mat: a stacked 'Don't Do This' label over lowering a baby straight onto the belly, then 'Do THIS instead' as the parent rolls the baby into tummy time, with the brand's Look at Me Ladybug toy as the focus object and a 'Follow for more' end card.

hook.visual: A woman kneeling on a play mat holds a baby upright against her chest and starts lowering the baby toward the floor; low phone angle, living room behind.
hook.on_screen_text: When starting Tummy Time ❌Don't Do This❌ (English on screen; no translation needed)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: it names a specific, everyday parent action (starting tummy time) and labels it as wrong in the first frame, which raises the worry 'am I doing this wrong?', while the demonstration is happening on screen so the viewer sees the mistake before reading it.

beats.observed: Woman lifts a baby upright against her chest with a hand across the baby's front and begins to lower. Two-tier label: 'When starting' over 'Tummy Time' on a black box, and a white pill reading '❌Don't Do This❌'.
beats.spoken: Transcript only has '(upbeat music)' for 0-2.6 s. No speech.
beats.on_screen_text: When starting Tummy Time | ❌Don't Do This❌

beats.observed: She places the baby face-down on the mat in one movement (hand under the chest at 1.5 s), the baby lies on the belly with the head turned near the mat (3.0 and 4.5 s) while her hand stays at the side or hip. Same label throughout.
beats.on_screen_text: When starting Tummy Time | ❌Don't Do This❌

beats.observed: Label flips at 6.0 s to a white pill with a green tick: '✅ Do THIS instead' (THIS in green). The baby lies on the side while she guides the hips and legs (6.0 s), then rolls the baby toward the belly (7.5 and 9.0 s) with a new caption.
beats.on_screen_text: ✅ Do THIS instead | Roll them in (& out) of it!

beats.observed: The baby is propped on the forearms and belly with her hand supporting beneath (10.5 s); a red wooden ladybug toy with black spots on a wooden rail comes into the foreground and the baby looks at it while she smiles (12.0 and 13.5 s).
beats.on_screen_text: They ease into it & learn the motor patterns of rolling!

beats.observed: Second take (her hair is now down, versus tied up in the first 13.5 s, so this looks like a separate clip): she holds the baby's feet and hips and rolls the baby onto the side (15.0 and 16.5 s), then the baby lies on the belly watching the ladybug on the rail while she smiles (18.0 to 21.0 s). The caption has a gap at 15.0 s.
beats.on_screen_text: Gradually offer less support until they are rolling 👏👏👏

beats.observed: She leans in and kisses the baby on the cheek; the ladybug is at the left edge of frame.
beats.on_screen_text: Follow for more baby development tips!

payoff: The 'do this' answer arrives at about 6.0 s (26% into the video); the rationale ('ease into it & learn the motor patterns of rolling') at about 10.5 s; the progression tip ('gradually offer less support') at about 16.5 s.
cta: On screen at the end: 'Follow for more baby development tips!'. Caption: 'Drop your questions below!' and a product mention of the Look at Me Ladybug.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: parents of infants would save it as a how-to or send it to a partner ('do it this way'). Only 17 comments on 409K views, so the 'drop your questions' prompt did not drive discussion.
why_it_worked: Wrong-vs-right demo in the first 6 s with two stacked text labels (❌ then ✅) that carry the full advice with the sound off; 409,372 views is 5.9x the account median of 69,791.

The product appears only as the helper in the fix (the ladybug holds the baby's gaze from 12 s), so it reads as a tip, not an ad; 3,426 likes is a 0.84% like rate (inferred: soft product placement tolerated).
Low-effort proof on screen: the same room, a real baby and a visible progression across about 23 s; comments are only 17, so the lift is from reach and saves, not conversation (inferred).
paid_signal: unclear: like_rate_pct 0.84 is above the 0.3 paid pattern, but the very low comments (17 on 409K views) and a branded product are consistent with a boosted or algorithm-pushed post; no direct evidence.

solo_route.how: 1) Get a barter expert (pediatric physio, OT or early-literacy specialist) to supply one safe 'Don't / Do' tip tied to a LumeBook moment, for example a bedtime-reading technique, and have them approve the exact on-screen wording. 2) Film hands-only or over-the-shoulder on a phone propped at floor level with a relative's child with written parental consent, or use the expert's own footage with permission. 3) In CapCut build the same two-label structure: black box 'When [doing X]' plus a white pill '❌Don't Do This❌' for the first 5 s, switch to '✅ Do THIS instead' by 6 s, then one explanation caption and one progression caption, ending on 'Follow for more'. 4) Use the LumeBook printed book as the focus object in the 'Do' half, the way the ladybug is used here.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert who signs off the tip (this is physical-development style advice, so do not copy the claims without expert review), a child plus parental consent, nothing else.

lumebook_version.hook_he: כשמקריאים לפעוט, אל תעשו את זה
lumebook_version.concept: A 20 second hands demo with the same stacked labels: ❌ reading straight through at speed, then ✅ pausing on the page where the child is the hero and asking them to point at themselves, with the LumeBook book as the visible object and an expert-approved one-line reason on screen.

evidence_notes: Observed: all three sheets (0 to 22.5 s) and single frames at 0, 4.5, 6, 15 and 22.5 s; on-screen English text read directly from frames. Spoken: whisper.srt only contains '(upbeat music)' at 0-2.6 s, so there is no usable speech transcript and I cannot say whether the presenter speaks. Text-change times are accurate to about plus or minus 1.5 s (frames every 1.5 s); the caption gap at 15.0 s and hair change between 13.5 and 15.0 s are observed. The Look at Me Ladybug name comes from the caption; the presenter is not named in the caption or on screen, so I do not identify her and cannot tell if she is staff, an expert or a creator (made_by unclear). No creator handle or collab credit is visible, so I found no sign of a repost. The baby's age is not stated.
